## Associated functions

<h3 id="new-keyed"><code>NewKeyed</code></h3>

```rux
pub func NewKeyed(key: char8[..]) -> Blake3
```

A keyed BLAKE3 hash: a message authentication code.
`key` must be exactly thirty-two bytes; a shorter one is padded with zeros, which is a caller error
rather than a supported shortening — a key with less entropy than the algorithm expects is weaker than
it looks, and padding it hides that rather than fixing it.
Unlike SHA-2, this needs no nested construction: BLAKE3 resists length extension, so starting the tree
from the key is a sound MAC on its own.

| Name  | Type        | Description |
| ----- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `key` | `char8[..]` | the key     |

**Returns**: a hasher keyed with those thirty-two bytes

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Blake3.rux#L46)

<h3 id="new-derive-key"><code>NewDeriveKey</code></h3>

```rux
pub func NewDeriveKey(context: char8[..]) -> Blake3
```

A BLAKE3 state deriving output under `context`.
The context string names what the derived key is _for_, and it is hashed separately from the key
material so that two derivations from the same material under different contexts are unrelated. It
should be a hard-coded, globally unique string — an application name, a purpose, and a date — and it
must not be a variable, since two callers who accidentally share one lose the separation entirely.

| Name      | Type        | Description                                                       |
| --------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `context` | `char8[..]` | the application-specific context string, which must be a constant |

**Returns**: a hasher in key-derivation mode for that context

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Blake3.rux#L60)

<h3 id="finish"><code>Finish</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Finish(self: &var Blake3, into: var char8[..])
```

Writes the root output into `into`, which may be any length.
BLAKE3's output is extendable like SHAKE's: the root compression repeats with an increasing counter to
produce as many bytes as asked. Thirty-two is the usual choice and is what [`DigestLength`](/docs/api/crypto/blake3#digest-length) reports.

| Name   | Type            | Description         |
| ------ | --------------- | ------------------- |
| `into` | `var char8[..]` | receives the output |

<h3 id="blake3-compress"><code>Blake3Compress</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Blake3Compress(chaining: *uint32, message: *uint32, counter: uint64, blockLength: uint32, flags: uint32, into: *var uint32)
```

The compression function: sixteen words of state over seven rounds, producing sixteen words of output.
The first eight output words are the chaining value; all sixteen are used when the output is being extended.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Blake3.rux#L76)

**Methods**

<h4 id="blake3-chunk-update"><code>Update</code></h4>

```rux
pub func Update(self: &var Blake3Chunk, bytes: char8[..]) -> uint
```

Adds bytes to the chunk, compressing whole blocks as they complete.
A block is only compressed once the _next_ byte arrives, never when it merely becomes full: the last
block of a chunk carries the end flag, and which block is last is not known until the chunk stops
growing. Compressing eagerly is the classic way to get the flags wrong.

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to absorb |

**Returns**: how many bytes were absorbed

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Crypto/Src/Blake3.rux#L197)
